absent: The 8250 table capacity, the initial active count, the full port and driver structure definitions, and the meaning of quirk and capability flags
Polling timeout computation, backup and normal timeout actions, shared interrupt chain join and leave mechanics, and ISA port initialization
Common console write, setup and exit behavior, early console option parsing, and console registration and power management contracts
Serial core publication, suspension and matching contracts plus RS485, modem GPIO, DMA, divisor, trigger, termios and emulation callback semantics
PL011 hardware offsets, flag encodings, FIFO thresholds, interrupt clearing, DMA control and vendor extension register use
Lock ordering between the global mutex and per-port locks, interrupt context constraints, and lifetime rules for private data and device pointers

findings.text: The core exposes a helper that returns the address of the global 8250 port table entry for a given line number, plus an initializer that validates the index against the table capacity, assigns line identity, captures shared operation vectors on first use, arms a per-port timer and installs driver callbacks before returning the slot or null when out of range.

Registration covers bulk publishing of early ports and single-port insertion or removal under a global mutex. Bulk publishing skips special infrared ports and already bound entries. Single insertion validates the clock, reuses a matching or free slot or extends the active count, preserves console flow state, copies addressing and callback configuration, applies quirks and publishes through the serial core, while removal detaches and optionally restores an unprobed placeholder when legacy ISA devices exist.

An early setup routine copies caller supplied addressing, clocking, sizing and optional IO handlers into the indexed table slot after range checks. Suspend and resume routines wrap core power callbacks with console specific handling for modem status work gating and scratch register probing on suspend and high speed restoration plus pending status handling on resume.

The universal 8250 console appears under the serial device name with nonblocking behavior and buffered output support, exposing atomic and threaded write handlers, device lock and unlock handlers, plus setup, teardown and early match handlers and a link to the driver descriptor. It starts with an invalid index and is registered at init when at least one port exists.

Console setup normalizes an out of range index, grows the active port count to cover the requested index, associates the port with the console object and invokes common setup, clearing the association on failure. Matching accepts only the expected early name, parses transport type and address from options, scans active ports for compatible transport and address equality and on success binds and initializes the found port.

The 8250 port store is a fixed capacity array whose valid indices are below the compile time maximum and whose active prefix length is tracked separately. Each active slot carries matching line and identifier values equal to its position, shares a common operation vector after first initialization and owns a private timer and driver callback table.

A port counts as a registered console only when it is flagged as a console and its linked console object is registered. The link itself is updated under the port lock, the console index selects the corresponding table slot for all console operations, and the driver descriptor holds either the console address or null depending on build configuration.

All console device locking, console link updates, modem status gating, pending status handling, overrun recovery and managed serial emulation teardown hold the per-port spinlock with interrupt state preserved. The small inline helpers centralize this discipline by wrapping the port lock acquisition and release.

Insertion, removal and slot search for 8250 ports are serialized by a dedicated global mutex, ensuring that matching, extension of the active count and publication or withdrawal through the serial core appear atomic with respect to each other.

The PL011 variant descriptor groups a register offset table, a default FIFO level, selectors for busy and modem signal flag bits plus an inversion mask, a set of boolean capability toggles covering access width and behavioral workarounds, and an optional callback that reports FIFO depth for a given bus device.

PL011 register addressing uses an abstract index space that distinguishes data, status, control, baud, FIFO and interrupt roles plus vendor extension slots and terminates with a size marker. The standard variant maps the common roles to hardware offsets while leaving vendor slots unmapped, with receive and transmit line control sharing one offset.

The 8250 driver descriptor identifies ownership, driver and device names, major and minor numbering and an optional console link. The driver operation table binds interrupt setup, interrupt release and timer setup handlers, and the base operation pointer preserves the first observed port operation vector for shared use.

Interrupt and timer provisioning depends on hardware capability. Ports with a transmit holding quirk arm an additional backup timer with an extended delay. Ports without a hardware interrupt rely on periodic polling, while ports with an interrupt join a shared chain. Release always cancels the timer synchronously, restores the normal timeout handler and leaves the chain only when an interrupt exists.

Slot selection for a new 8250 description prefers an exact transport match, then the requested line when still untouched, then the earliest untouched slot, then any slot still marked unknown, reporting absence when none qualifies.

Console suspend forbids new modem status work under lock and waits for in-flight work before invoking core suspend, with an optional scratch register integrity probe when suspend output remains enabled on nonstandard hardware. Resume clears the probe marker, restores high speed configuration on capable hardware, invokes core resume and then reallows work while draining any saved modem changes.
Overrun recovery is deferred to a delayed work item that under lock reenables receive status interrupts and propagates the updated mask to the interrupt enable register.

Out of range indices, zero clocks, missing slots, incompatible console indices and unmatched early descriptions all fail without side effects beyond defined cleanup such as clearing a tentative console link or detaching private state. Special infrared ports are never published, and fixed type requests bypass auto detection.

Runtime power acquisition occurs only for already registered consoles, modem signal GPIO setup is skipped for devices with firmware companions and errors there or in RS485 mode parsing abort insertion. Transmit load size defaults from FIFO size and line status mask defaults from a shared constant when unspecified, and delayed overrun work is created only when a positive backoff interval is configured.

The PL011 support fixes the port count at 14 with major 204 and minor 64 and the same count for the serial alias, bounds interrupt service passes at 256, defines the data error mask as the combination of overrun, break, parity and framing indicators, and reserves bit 16 for synthetic receive marking.

The 8250 driver uses device name ttyS with minor 64 under the standard TTY major, and its console uses the same name with print buffer, anytime and nonblocking flags and an initial index of minus one. Early matching recognizes the four letter uart name.

The ARM variant uses standard offsets, a combined receive and transmit FIFO threshold, busy plus modem flag selectors and revision dependent FIFO depth of 16 below revision 3 and 32 otherwise. The server and QDF variants use 32 bit access with always enabled and fixed option behavior, and the QDF variant inverts busy detection by treating transmit empty as busy.
Resume on National Semiconductor capable hardware restores the UART clock to 921600 multiplied by 16, and suspend probing uses marker value decimal 165.

Conversion from generic port to 8250 extension uses container linkage through the embedded port member. Register output delegates to the per-port output callback, and console flow state is stored as a simple boolean with paired accessors that preserve existing enablement across reconfiguration.
